body.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). For every regular real \(\Sigma\succ0\) outside \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\), the algorithm returns \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\) for each simple real root \(z\) of \(p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\), and \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\) accepts if and only if \(z\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). For every accepted complete real supported \(\Lambda\), the recovered matrix \(\Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\) is positive definite by congruence; positivity of \(\Omega\) is a conclusion and is not an antecedent of the lifting criterion.
body.justification: Complex degree is not a real ambiguity count, so root-by-root extension is required before a causal coefficient value is reported.
body.gap: Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant separate real positive-definite fibers from complex genericity, and Bouzidi et al. isolate real solutions; the missing result is an if-and-only-if supported-SEM lift for each projected coordinate root.
body.consumer: Applied SEM analysts receive all and only real structural explanations of a regular observed covariance, without a false uniqueness conclusion from local rank.

obligation.what_is_open: The advertised finite if-and-only-if real-extension certificate for every regular specialization, especially on positive-dimensional fibers and recorded pole divisors.
obligation.obstruction: The arithmetic model has no finite encoding for an arbitrary real covariance, and the available bivariate rational-univariate source does not cover real feasibility of every positive-dimensional incidence stratum.
obligation.attempted: I proved the exact residual criterion and the positive-definiteness conclusion by congruence, but neither supplies the missing finite real sample-point certificate.
obligation.partial_result:
For any complete real supported lift, acyclicity makes \(R=I_n-\Lambda\) invertible and
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Omega x=x^{\mathsf T}R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma Rx=(Rx)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(Rx)>0
\]
for \(x\ne0\). Hence \(\Omega\succ0\), and the missing residual equations are exactly its required zero entries. Thus a real root is retained exactly when its semialgebraic incidence fiber has a real point. The unresolved part is the finite \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\): arbitrary real covariances have no finite encoding in the frozen arithmetic model, and positive-dimensional pole divisors are not covered by the cited bivariate rational-univariate machinery.
